message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that Canadians enjoyed in 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday (or is observed on the nearest weekday when it lands on a weekend), giving you a three‑day break that includes the weekend.

| Date(s) | Holiday | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 1 – Jan 3** | New Year’s Day (observed Jan 2) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, so the holiday was observed on Monday, giving a 3‑day break (Sat 1 – Mon 2). |
| **Feb 18 – Feb 20** | Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Family Day is always on the 3rd Monday of February. |
| **Apr 7 – Apr 9** | Good Friday | Good Friday is a statutory holiday on the Friday before Easter Sunday. |
| **May 19 – May 21** | Victoria Day | Celebrated on the Monday preceding May 25. |
| **Jul 1 – Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed Jul 3) | Canada Day fell on Saturday, so the holiday was observed on Monday, giving a 3‑day break (Sat 1 – Mon 3). |
| **Sep 2 – Sep 4** | Labour Day | First Monday in September. |
| **Oct 7 – Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Second Monday in October. |
| **Nov 9 – Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Observed on Monday, Nov 11. |
| **Dec 23 – Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Christmas Day fell on Monday, giving a 3‑day break (Sat 23 – Mon 25). |

### Quick‑look calendar view

```
Jan 2023
 1 (Sun) New Year’s Day (observed Mon 2)
Feb 2023
 20 (Mon) Family Day
Apr 2023
 7 (Fri) Good Friday
May 2023
 21 (Mon) Victoria Day
Jul 2023
 1 (Sat) Canada Day (observed Mon 3)
Sep 2023
 4 (Mon) Labour Day
Oct 2023
 9 (Mon) Thanksgiving
Nov 2023
 11 (Mon) Remembrance Day
Dec 2023
 25 (Mon) Christmas Day
```

> **Tip for your holiday‑planning app:**  
> • Store the holiday dates in UTC or ISO‑8601 format (`YYYY-MM-DD`).  
> • Flag holidays that are “observed” on a different day (e.g., Canada Day 2023 → 2023‑07‑03).  
> • If you need province‑specific holidays (e.g., Family Day in Ontario vs. St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland), keep a separate lookup table per province.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the same information broken down by province or if you need additional holidays (e.g., provincial holidays that don’t create long weekends).
